pr_title: Improved error handling and recovery during compaction and metadata log replay
pr_body:
Fixes #9336
##### Summary
Add additional checks 

1. Recover from possible missing chart GUID compaction records that can result to incomplete metadata log replay information
    - When a dimension compaction request is received  a check will ensure that it's chart is also *force compacted* if needed
1. Metric GUID generation to detects and recovers from collisions (caused by inconsistent metadata log information)
   - This can happen when a corrupted metadata log file already exists due to case 1
1. Log unsuccessful GUID context switch (also due to corrupted metadata log file due to case 1)

##### Component Name
database

##### Test Plan

review_comments: Are you putting a `switch(ret)` inside a shared case in a `switch(ret)` to avoid repeating the `host = ` line above ??
This is a remnant from the persistent metadata feature branch. It used to have a lot of code about hosts but it got cleaned up and the monstrosity remained.

This should be an impossible state. You can't have a dbengine dimension without a UUID, it has to fail here or it will fail later. The collectors expect to be able to use dimensions, there is no other failure mode here unfortunately.

Just because it should be impossible is not a strong enough reason. If it was actually impossible then it would be valid to ignore it. If we have code to trap it thenit just seems to be unlikely, which is not the same. If something goes wrong - what is the least harmful way of dealing with it?
Why not mark the dimension as disabled / in error - and allow the agent to continue?

When I detect state corruption I prefer to fail fast, before propagating the corruption to other components. This way it's easier to debug and you can do less damage to user data. That's my personal preference though.

In some systems that is desirable, especially if they are short-lived and interactive (e.g. command line tools). In others it can be quite harmful. We should aim for graceful degradation of service, and best-effort delivery where possible. In this specific case - what can cause the generation attempt to fail - and what does it tell us about the state of the system? i.e. does it make sense to continue, does it make sense to abort.

In this specific case  (i.e. after the collision has been detected) it will only fail if the newly generated GUID already exists in the map i.e. we have managed to generate a duplicate GUID.

In case of memory allocation errors with mallocz or JudyHSIns error,  it will never return because fatal() is called.
That seems insanely unlikely. Why not just repeat it if that happens instead of aborting the agent?
Should this case continue instead of returning NULL?
This seems wrong - if the GUID in the context command was a dimension then why treat it as a chart?

We don't have a dimension state yet, in theory you could add dimension labels in this context and set `rd=dimension`, `st=dimension's chart`, `host=chart's host`.

Since the only state we have right now is `st`, we just set this.
